_readme: Brands we have NOT tested. Facts come only from each brand's own pages on the 'checked' date. Update prices here; alternatives pages rebuild from this file and data/bench.json. hw = hardware per radio at the smallest pack; renew = per radio per year after year 1; monthly = per radio per month (billed from day one).

rapid-radios.name: Rapid Radios
rapid-radios.maker: Rapid Radios, a Grand Rapids, Michigan company (part of Rapid Consulting LLC)
rapid-radios.priceText: $399 per 2-pack (about $200 a radio), on Rapid Radios' site and Amazon
rapid-radios.renewText: First year included, then $50 per radio per year ($40 with auto-pay)
facts: $399 per 2-pack on rapidradios.com and Amazon; packs up to 10 radios ($1,495)
First year included; then $50 per radio per year, or $40 on auto-pay; no monthly bill
Multi-carrier SIM that connects to Verizon, AT&T or T-Mobile
8800 mAh listed, USB-C, "5+ days" standby claimed
RAD1 (LTE + Wi-Fi, IPX6 listed) from $399 for one radio; a base/car unit for $299
stayIf: You want a US company with a Michigan phone line to call when something goes wrong.
You want one SIM that can use any of the three big US carriers.
You want a matching base or car unit from the same brand.

peakptt.name: PeakPTT
peakptt.maker: Peak PTT, a US business push-to-talk provider
peakptt.priceText: $229 per radio, plus $19.95 activation and $24.95 per radio per month
peakptt.renewText: $24.95 per radio per month from activation, month to month
facts: $229 per radio, plus a $19.95 activation fee per radio
$24.95 per radio per month, billed from activation; month to month, no contract
GPS tracking portal included; dispatch seat $12/month; phone app $9.95/user/month
5200 mAh listed, 8–12 hours of use claimed
stayIf: You need every radio on a live GPS map with a dispatcher console.
You want one company handling hardware, airtime and support on a business account.
You'd rather pay monthly and cancel anytime than buy a year of service up front.
